title: Seeing Like a Computer: Facebook's Automatic Alternative Text

description.main: An artist's book that sets images from Mark Zuckerberg's Facebook Wall beside the machine-generated alt text Facebook attached to them. The captions read like "one person, smiling" or "person, outdoor, nature."
description.extended:
A book of the automatic captions Facebook's image recognition wrote for pictures on Mark Zuckerberg's own Wall.

The captions come from Automatic Alternative Text, a feature meant to give screen-reader users more context. They are not shown on the page. They sit in each image's alt tag in the HTML. Waller sets them beside the pictures they describe: "one person, smiling," "person, outdoor, nature." The publisher says the fragments suit Zuckerberg's public persona while hiding the content and context of the images. The paperback has 209 pages and measures 23 x 16.5 cm. Unknown Unknowns published it in 2018.

Angie Waller is the artist and designer behind the project. Her own site lists the book as a September 2018 publication and points to Unknown Unknowns for purchase.

notes: Page count differs by source: the publisher lists 209 pages, one retailer lists 217. Identified from a spine photograph; edition not checked against the copy.
